definitions.explanation: A variety of language spoken in a particular region that differs from the standard language in vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{関西|かんさい}{方言|ほうげん}を{話|はな}す。
この{言葉|ことば}は{東北|とうほく}{地方|ちほう}の{方言|ほうげん}です。
examples.english: This word is from the Tohoku dialect.

examples.japanese: {方言|ほうげん}には{地域|ちいき}の{文化|ぶんか}が{反映|はんえい}されている。
examples.english: Dialects reflect the culture of their regions.

notes:
JAPANESE DIALECTS:
Japan has many regional dialects, broadly categorized as:

- {関西弁|かんさいべん} - Kansai dialect (Osaka, Kyoto area)
- {東北弁|とうほくべん} - Tohoku dialect (northeastern Japan)
- {九州弁|きゅうしゅうべん} - Kyushu dialect
- {北海道弁|ほっかいどうべん} - Hokkaido dialect
- {沖縄方言|おきなわほうげん} - Okinawan dialects

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {方言|ほうげん}を{話|はな}す - to speak a dialect
- {方言|ほうげん}が{出|で}る - dialect comes out (unintentionally)
- {方言|ほうげん}が{強|つよ}い - to have a strong dialect
- お{国|くに}{言葉|ことば} - regional speech (more casual/affectionate term)

RELATED WORDS:
- {標準語|ひょうじゅんご} - standard language
- {訛|なま}り - accent, dialect influence
- {共通語|きょうつうご} - common language
- {土地|とち}{言葉|ことば} - local speech

CULTURAL NOTE:
Dialects are increasingly valued as cultural heritage. Many people use dialect with family and friends while speaking {標準語|ひょうじゅんご} in formal settings.

REGISTER:
Neutral. Standard term for academic and everyday use.
